conventions.convention: Complex Hilbert inner products are linear in the first variable. Self-adjointness includes equality of operator domains.
The resolvent spectral PVM is extended to ambient Borel sets by intersection with its spectrum. E_B({0})=0 does not imply 0 is absent from the spectrum.
Hermite indices belong to N₀²; the unscaled oscillator is H=−Δ+|x|² and its eigenvalues are 2|α|+2.
The field is real, two-dimensional and massive with m>0. Its Fourier transform uses exp(−ip·x), inverse factor (2π)⁻², and covariance multiplier (|p|²+m²)⁻¹.

The random distribution takes values in the continuous real-linear Schwartz dual equipped with the evaluation-generated cylinder sigma-algebra; the theorem supplies a common full-measure set of tempered samples, not pointwise field values.

The Lorentz brackets are [J_i,J_j]=ε_ijk J_k, [J_i,K_j]=ε_ijk K_k and [K_i,K_j]=−ε_ijk J_k, with ε_123=1. Both the representation and cocycle are real-linear, and the coefficient space is finite-dimensional complex.
AC is assumed for spectral calculus and Gaussian-field existence; the Hermite decay lemma assumes Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. For a densely defined nonnegative self-adjoint A on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, B=(I+A)⁻¹ is a bounded positive self-adjoint injection with dense range, spectrum in [0,1], and E_B({0})=0. Pushing its PVM forward through b↦b⁻¹−1 gives A with domain exactly {u: ∫λ² dμ_u<∞}; bounded Borel functions satisfy the stated operator-norm bound and quadratic identity.

Assume AC and m>0. There is a probability measure on the cylinder sigma-algebra of the continuous real-linear Schwartz dual on R² whose evaluation vectors are centered jointly Gaussian and satisfy E[Φ(f)Φ(g)]=C_m(f,g), with the stated massive Fourier covariance. The construction gives tempered-distribution samples on one common full-measure set.
For the stated real Lorentz Lie algebra, every real-linear cocycle c into a finite-dimensional complex representation V satisfies c(X)=ρ(X)v for some v∈V and every X.

Assume Countable Choice. For every integer r≥0 and complex Schwartz function f on R², the stated product Hermite basis satisfies ∑α(1+|α|)^(2r)|⟨f,h_α⟩|² ≤ ‖H^r f‖²₂ < ∞. The coefficient map is continuous into each corresponding weighted square-summable sequence space.

published_dependencies.used_for: Explicit choice hypothesis for the spectral theorem, Kolmogorov extension and the counterexample.
Countable-family choice hypothesis of PVM calculus and Hilbert/Hermite suppliers; inherited from AC where required.
Projection, normalization, intersection, strong countable-additivity and regularity conventions.
Bounded spectral integrals, norm bounds and quadratic identities used in truncation arguments.
Multiplicativity, adjoints and uniformly bounded strong convergence of spectral multipliers.
Existence and uniqueness of the regular spectral PVM for the bounded resolvent under AC.
Resolvent lower bounds, adjoint-domain bounds and square-summable-series estimates.
Ambient-norm bounded-functional characterization of the unbounded adjoint, including its domain.
Complete product Hermite basis and oscillator eigenvalues at N=2 and a₁=a₂=c=1.
Norm-convergent orthonormal expansions and Parseval identities.
Polynomial-Gaussian representatives and their derivative decay for integration by parts.
Identification of the precise unscaled two-dimensional product basis and eigenvalues.
Admissibility of real Gaussian coordinate spaces in Kolmogorov extension.
Underlying test-function space and polynomial derivative seminorms.
Continuity of the sample functionals and covariance square-root multiplier.
Identification of limits of Gaussian finite sums with centered normal laws.
Exact 2π-normalized supplier convention and its conversion to momentum p.
Normalization and characteristic functions of scalar Gaussian laws.
Consistency of finite product Gaussian marginals.
Construction of the countable family of independent Gaussian coordinates on the cylinder sigma-algebra.
Covariance calculation with the exact Fourier normalization.
Continuity and Schwartz preservation of the massive covariance square-root operator.
Induced round metric used in the compact-group averaging construction.
Round sphere geometry for the explicit SU(2) averaging integral.
Coordinate density √det G and its absolute-Jacobian convention.
Compactly supported chart integrals in the averaging construction.
Integrability of continuous compactly supported chart integrands on bounding rectangles.
Partition independence and left invariance of the explicitly constructed round-volume integral.
Compactness of S³ in the Lorentz cocycle proof.
